event: "Fine. A bit boring, but it should be fast." Nala tucks her papers away and leaves the Moot Hall.
On the square she stops at a carter's wagon and a wine factor's stall and asks after Voss's men.
The carter shrugs: he came up the south road, and has heard nothing from the east.
The wine factor has heard only the taproom tale: a woman hunter took Voss's head. He eyes her sword.

memory.fact: On day 9 a wine factor on the square repeats the taproom tale of a woman hunter taking Voss's head.

event: She asks two more traders on the way down to the west gate; neither has any word of the crew.

memory.fact: No other trader in Wendlow or on the road today has word of Voss's crew since he fell.

event: At the west gate the watchman sees her badge and waves her out with a nod.
The road runs west along the Wend's bank under a high afternoon sun, farmland on either side.
Three miles out, a wool cart comes the other way behind a grey ox, its carter walking at its head.
He is a lean, sunburned man, and gives his name as Jory Webb, bound for Wendlow's market.

memory.fact: On day 9, west of Wendlow, an eastbound wool carter, Jory Webb, meets Nala on the road.
On day 9, west of Wendlow, an eastbound wool carter, Jory Webb, meets Nala on the road.

event: Asked about trouble on the road, he spits. "Paid a silver toll on day seven, near Fenwatch."
"One man alone, with a crossbow. Stepped out of the trees and held it on me till I paid."
"Talked like a northerner, that burr they have. Hard-faced. Didn't give a name."

memory.fact: Jory was tolled a silver on day 7 near Fenwatch by a lone crossbowman with a northern burr.
Jory was tolled a silver on day 7 near Fenwatch by a lone crossbowman with a northern burr.

event: "Thought the quarry lot were finished. Seems one of them's set up on his own."

memory.fact: Jory Webb reckons one of Voss's crew has set up tolling the road on his own.
